note:
Malcolm: the heap is worse — stack three or four of the cream pots instead, on the graphite background.

WHY THIS SHOULD SOLVE THE LETTERING. The approved range_stacked_jars shots already in publish-ready render every jar label correctly — 'COPPER PEPTIDE / ADVANCED DAY REPAIR / PREMIUM FORMULA / DAY CREAM | 2% GHK-CU | 50ML' is crisp and right on all four products. The jar carries five short lines; the carton carries the same five plus benefit strings and side panels. Less copy per surface, and one surface per object instead of three, is exactly the condition under which the earlier arrangements held together. The fine-print instruction from the cream-carton brief is kept anyway.

GEOMETRY, MEASURED NOT DESCRIBED. Each jar is 1.15 times wider than its full height, and the lid band is a third of that height. A stack is jar-on-lid, so those two ratios set the whole column. Stating them beats 'squat jar', which drifts.

Four distinct glass colours, so no two jars in the stack read alike: deep navy, pale ice-blue, neutral white, soft pink. All four lids are the same neutral brushed silver — the specs are emphatic that they never go rose-gold, copper or champagne.

slots.title: Four cream pots stacked into a column, graphite
slots.prompt: Studio photograph of exactly four Skingenetix cream jars from the reference images, stacked squarely one on top of another into a single neat upright column in the centre of a tall portrait frame. Every jar is the same size and shape: a frosted glass cosmetic jar 1.15 times wider than its full height, with a brushed satin neutral silver-grey screw lid forming a tall band a third of that height. Each jar sits flat and centred on the lid of the one below, front labels aligned and square to camera, the column standing straight and level, nothing tilted or leaning. From top to bottom the glass colours are: pale ice-blue, then neutral frosted white, then soft rose-pink, then deep navy blue at the base. All four lids are the same neutral brushed silver-grey, never rose-gold, copper, champagne or chrome. Legible type, and nothing else, reads on the front labels: on the pale ice-blue jar the Skingenetix DNA-helix mark with the wordmark 'Skingenetix', then 'COPPER PEPTIDE', then 'ADVANCED NIGHT REPAIR'. On the white jar the same mark and wordmark, then 'MATRIXYL 3000 PRO COLLAGEN', then 'FULL & FIRMING TREATMENT'. On the pink jar the same mark and wordmark, then 'PDRN COLLAGEN REPAIR', then 'DEEP RENEWAL TREATMENT'. On the navy jar the same mark and wordmark, then 'COPPER PEPTIDE', then 'ADVANCED DAY REPAIR'. Every remaining line on every label is fine print far too small to read - render it as fine unreadable print, never as placeholder words, never as invented wording, and print nothing that is not quoted here. A single hard key light from the upper left with one soft fill, throwing one clean defined shadow of the whole column down and to the right across a smooth seamless graphite surface, colour #1A1A1A, that fills the background evenly. Premium skincare campaign still life, crisp focus across the front labels, physically based frosted glass and brushed aluminium.
